places.title: Ascension Cathedral
places.why: One of the tallest wooden churches in the world, built of Tian Shan spruce on a frame designed to ride out earthquakes: it came through the 1911 quake that levelled much of Verny. Its pastel walls, onion domes and tall bell tower close the main alley of Panfilov Park.

places.title: Panfilov Park
places.why: The old city garden of Verny, an 18-hectare grid of elms, oaks and firs between Kunaev, Gogol, Zenkov and Kazybek bi streets. The Ascension Cathedral, the Memorial of Glory and the wooden Officers’ Assembly stand along its alleys.

photos.file: Park named after Panfilov’s 28 guardsmen, 2013 year..jpg
photos.author: SkySex

photos.file: Panfilov's Twenty-Eight Guardsmen Park, Almaty, Kazakhstan.jpg
photos.author: Behrami

places.title: Green Bazaar (Kok Bazar)
places.why: The central market of the city in a large late-Soviet hall, with stalls of horse meat, dried fruit, kurt and Korean salads; a daily slice of city life a block from the Arbat.

photos.author: Stefan Krasowski from New York, NY, USA

places.title: Medeu High-Altitude Skating Rink
places.architect: Vladimir Katsev, Arystan Kainarbaev; engineer S. Matveev
places.why: An open-air speed-skating stadium at 1691 m in a mountain gorge above the city, its concrete stands built into the slopes and backed by the great mudflow dam. Its architects received the USSR State Prize; the rink and dam are on Kazakhstan’s UNESCO Tentative List.

photos.author: Stefan Krasowski from New York, NY, USA

places.title: Shymbulak
places.why: A ski and hiking area at 2200–2500 m reached by a gondola from Medeu, with chair lifts on to the Talgar Pass at about 3200 m and views across the peaks of the Zailiysky Alatau.

places.title: Kok-Tobe
places.architect: TV tower: N. Terzieva, A. Savchenko, N. Akimov
places.why: A green hill at 1130 m on the edge of the centre, reached by a cable car from beside the Palace of the Republic over the old garden district. From the top the whole city spreads out against the mountains; the latticed TV tower stands just above.

places.title: Republic Square and Independence Monument
places.architect: M. Pavlov, A. Kapanov, K. Montakhaev, R. Seidalin, Yu. Tumanyan; monument: Shot-Aman Valikhanov
places.area: between Dostyk Avenue and Zheltoksan Street
places.why: The ceremonial square of the Soviet capital, framed by the Akimat and by symmetric towers and office blocks, with a long view to the mountains. Its column carrying the Golden Man on a winged snow leopard marks Kazakhstan’s independence.

photos.file: Площадь Республики в Алматы. Июль, 2015 года.JPG
photos.author: Меридианец

places.title: Arbat (Zhibek Zholy pedestrian street)
places.area: Zhibek Zholy, between Abylai Khan Avenue and Kunaev Street
places.why: The city’s first pedestrian street, a shady promenade of street musicians, painters and cafés running past the TsUM department store towards the Green Bazaar.

places.title: Panfilov Street promenade
places.area: Panfilov Street, between Zhibek Zholy and Kabanbai Batyr
places.why: A central street turned into a walking boulevard in 2017, following ideas of the Danish urbanist Jan Gehl: wide paving under old trees, benches and café terraces from the Arbat down to the Opera.

places.title: Hotel Kazakhstan
places.architect: Yuri Ratushny, Lev Ukhobotov, A. Anchugov, V. Kashtanov
places.why: The first high-rise in the Soviet Union built in a nine-point seismic zone: a 26-storey tower crowned by a golden openwork crown that became a symbol of the city.

places.title: Palace of the Republic
places.architect: Nikolai Ripinsky, Vladimir Kim, Lev Ukhobotov, Yuri Ratushny
places.why: A concert hall under a wide, floating roof with Kazakh-inspired forms, set on a terraced square with fountains and the Abai monument. The design won the USSR State Prize in 1971; a rebuild in 2010–2011 changed much of its skin.

photos.file: Дворец Республики во время проведения форума New Vision.jpg
photos.author: MaxKNV

places.title: Abai Opera and Ballet Theatre
places.why: A classical theatre of the 1930s capital whose arcades, loggias and capitals are worked with Kazakh ornament, standing at the head of a square with the mountains behind.

places.title: Old Square and the former House of Government
places.why: The government seat of Soviet Kazakhstan, a long palace with a columned portico over the old central square, built to resist earthquakes. Now the Kazakh-British Technical University, it is on the UNESCO Tentative List with the cathedral and Hotel Kazakhstan.

places.title: Academy of Sciences
places.architect: Alexei Shchusev; completed by Nikolai Prostakov
places.why: A palace of Stalin-era classicism by the architect of Lenin’s Mausoleum, whose portals and ornament borrow from the madrasas of Central Asia.

photos.file: Qazaqstan Gylym Akademiasyna qarama qarsy ornalasqan Qylym ordasynyn artky zagy.jpg
photos.author: Bekbal

places.title: Arasan Baths
places.why: A public bathhouse treated as a palace: a long low block crowned by clusters of domes with skylights, after the bathhouses of Central Asia, with marble-lined halls inside.

places.title: Golden Square
places.area: central Almaty, between Abai Avenue and Zhibek Zholy
places.why: The quiet heart of the Soviet capital: a grid of streets shaded by old trees and lined with aryks, the open irrigation channels of the city, with houses of the 1930s to 1970s built for the Soviet elite.
places.note: The outline is the OSM neighbourhood of Golden Square; sources draw its edges differently (T—Zh: Kabanbai Batyr, Zheltoksan, Kunaev and Abai).

other.note: Abai Opera, which the Telegraph places in the Golden Quarter

places.title: Almaty Metro
places.area: Line 1, under Nazarbayev Avenue and Abai Avenue
places.why: A short, deep metro line whose stations each have a theme in stone, glass and metal: a stained-glass apple tree at Almaly, a Silk Road panel at Zhibek Zholy, a bronze relief of the poet at Abai, folk ornament at Raiymbek Batyr.

photos.author: Alex J. Butler from United Kingdom

places.title: Main Botanical Garden
places.why: A garden of more than 100 hectares at the foot of the mountains with trees from around the world, renewed in 2020 with a glass entrance pavilion, lily ponds and pergolas; one of the favourite walks of the city.

photos.file: 01 Центральный вход в Алматинский ботанический сад.jpg
photos.author: Marat Rysbekov

places.title: Tselinny Center of Contemporary Culture
places.architect: original: Saveliy Rosenblum, Vladimir Katsev; renovation: Asif Khan
places.why: A Thaw-era panoramic cinema, the first in the city with a glass front, rebuilt as an arts centre: the concrete frame and the sgraffito mural were kept, and a new facade of vertical fins and a cloud-like glass foyer open it to the street.

places.title: Officers’ Assembly (Ykylas Museum of Folk Musical Instruments)
places.why: A wooden building in the Russian revival style with steep roofs and carved details, by the builder of the cathedral. Built as the garrison officers’ club, it now holds a museum of Kazakh folk instruments.

places.title: Memorial of Glory
places.architect: Toleu Basenov, Rustem Seidalin; sculptors Anatoly Artimovich, Vladimir Andryushchenko
places.why: A Second World War memorial of three monumental bronze compositions with an eternal flame in front, one of the strongest works of late-Soviet monumental sculpture in Central Asia.

places.title: Kasteev State Museum of Arts
places.architect: E. Kuznetsova, B. Novikov, O. Naumova
places.why: The country’s main art museum in a modernist building of 1976, later crowned with a glass pyramid, with a sculpture garden in front.

photos.file: 108th AB Performs at Founders Museum Opening in Almaty (9779613).jpg
photos.author: U.S. Army National Guard photo by Sgt. 1st Class Jacob Dunlap

photos.file: Rooms of State Museum of Arts, Almaty 03.jpg
photos.author: Davide Mauro

places.title: Central State Museum of Kazakhstan
places.architect: Yuri Ratushny, Z. Mustafina, B. Rzagaliev
places.why: A late-Soviet museum composed like a cluster of white volumes around a central blue dome, a modern echo of Central Asian domed halls, home to the Saka gold of the region.

photos.file: Almaty Central State Museum of Kazakhstan, July 2025.jpg
photos.author: Nurken

places.title: Almaty Museum of Arts
places.why: A private museum of modern and contemporary art formed by two L-shaped volumes, one clad in limestone like the mountains behind, the other in aluminium like the city, with a top-lit street running between them.

photos.file: The Museum of Arts in Almaty.jpg
photos.author: Dauren Nabijan

places.title: Kyzyl-Tan (Gabdulvaliev Trading House)
places.architect: attributed to Paul Gourdet or Andrei Zenkov
places.why: A merchant’s shop of the Verny era with a richly carved wooden facade, small towers and a dome, one of the few such buildings left; it was restored after a fire in 2009.

places.title: Palace of Schoolchildren
places.architect: Vladimir Kim, A. Zuev, Tolegen Abilda
places.why: The former Pioneers’ Palace, a long white composition on a slope with an observatory tower like a minaret; its plan coils like a spiral galaxy, as it was first meant to house a museum of space.

places.title: Arman Cinema
places.architect: Alexander Korzhempo, V. Panin, I. Slonov
places.why: The first modernist cinema of the city and the last free-standing one still showing films: a glazed hall behind a heavy concrete entrance, with large reliefs by Konstantinov on its walls.

places.title: Hotel Almaty
places.architect: Nikolai Ripinsky, P. Kartasis, A. Kossov
places.why: A modernist slab beside the Opera with a large mosaic of the Enlik-Kebek legend at its base; a careful restoration of its facade brought back its 1960s look.

places.title: Natalia Sats Russian Theatre for Children and Youth
places.architect: A. Petrova, Z. Mustafina, G. Dzhakipova
places.why: The former Palace of Culture of the cotton mill, a brutalist block covered by a huge relief on the theme of the arts by Tverdokhlebov.

places.title: Wedding Palace
places.why: A modernist pavilion for civil weddings, with a mosaic of the Kyz Zhibek love legend on its walls.

places.title: House of Officers (Army House)
places.architect: Yuri Ratushny, Oleg Balykbaev, Tokhtar Eraliev
places.why: A monumental block of the 1970s beside Panfilov Park, with an imperial weight outside and a theatrical interior to match.

places.title: Museum of Almaty (former Verny orphanage)
places.why: A brick building of 1879 on a street corner, one of the oldest of the Verny era, built as the town orphanage and now the museum of the city’s history.

places.title: National Library of Kazakhstan
places.architect: Vladimir Ishchenko, Vladimir Kim et al.
places.why: A light-filled modernist library of 1970, one of the purest works of Almaty modernism and a monument of republican significance.

photos.file: National Library of the Republic of Kazakhstan in Almaty.jpg
photos.author: МаратД

photos.file: Kazakhstan Republic National library in Almaty.jpg
photos.author: МаратД

places.title: Main Post Office (House of Communications)
places.why: A constructivist building of the early 1930s, one of the first public buildings of the new capital of Soviet Kazakhstan.

places.title: House of Political Education on Dostyk Avenue
places.architect: Yuri Ratushny, Oleg Balykbaev, Tokhtar Eraliev
places.why: A late brutalist building near Republic Square with massive concrete walls and shaded openings; critics compare it with the work of Paul Rudolph.

places.title: Verny Men’s Gymnasium
places.why: The first secondary school of the town, a brick building by the first architect of Verny, now a university building.

places.title: Verny City School (Kolpakovsky School)
places.why: A school building of 1890, one of the oldest public buildings of Verny, a monument of republican significance.

places.title: Al-Farabi Kazakh National University campus
places.why: A university town on the slope south of the centre, built from the 1970s with concrete faculty blocks around a long axis and a tall rectorate.

places.title: St Nicholas Cathedral
places.why: A church of the Verny era with five onion domes and a tall bell tower, one of the landmarks of the western part of the centre.

photos.author: Brian Harrington Spier from Shanghai, China

places.title: Esentai Park (Esentai Tower and Apartments)
places.why: A tower with a faceted glass shaft, for some years the tallest building in Kazakhstan, and a residential complex by the same firm beside the Esentai river; the apartments won the national architecture award in 2015.

places.title: Three Bogatyrs
places.architect: A. Petrov, B. Churlyaev, V. Gershberg et al.
places.why: Three 12-storey towers set on a terrace above Dostyk Avenue, an early experiment with high-rise housing in a seismic city; the name comes from the three heroes of Russian folk tales.

places.title: Central Mosque
places.why: The largest mosque of the city, a white marble building of 1999 with a blue dome, decorated inside with Kazakh ornament.

places.title: Hotel Otrar
places.why: A hotel of 1981 facing Panfilov Park, whose facades carry reliefs and murals.

places.title: Shakhvorostov House
places.why: A merchant’s house of the Verny era in the Art Nouveau style, a monument of republican significance.

places.title: Twin towers on the Arbat (Bliznetsy)
places.why: A pair of 19-storey residential towers turned at 45 degrees to the street grid, their staggered balconies stacked like a game of Jenga above the Arbat.

places.title: First House of Government (Academy of Arts)
places.why: The constructivist seat of the young Kazakh republic by the leading theorist of Soviet modernism, built when the capital moved to Alma-Ata; much altered, now the Zhurgenov Academy of Arts.

places.title: Verny Women’s Gymnasium
places.why: A brick school of the late Verny period on a central corner, one of the surviving public buildings of the town.

places.title: Narxoz University
places.why: A 1970s campus with a large Soviet mosaic by Sebastian Kirakozov, whose main building was converted into a business school with a new, open interior in 2024.

places.title: Tchaikovsky Music College
places.why: A modernist school building known for its large mosaic by Evgeny Sidorkin, A. Danderfer and B. Bogomolov.

places.title: Former Ministry of Grain Products
places.why: A pale blue classical building with Corinthian columns from the first years of the Soviet capital; once the Book Museum, now a cultural centre.

places.title: Zhambyl Philharmonic
places.why: A concert hall of 1936, originally the House of Culture of the Kazakhfilm studio, on a quiet corner of the centre.

places.title: Golovizin House
places.area: Nazarbayev Avenue 162, corner of Kurmangazy Street
places.why: An Art Nouveau merchant’s house of the Verny era on a central corner, a monument of republican significance.

photos.file: Дом Т. А. Головизина, проспект Назарбаева, 162, Алма-Ата.jpg
photos.author: SAKRI

places.title: Akimat (City Hall)
places.why: The former Central Committee of the Communist Party, a long white brutalist block at the head of Republic Square. Damaged in January 2022 and restored.

photos.file: Акимат Алматы на Площади Республики. Июль, 2015 года.JPG
photos.author: Меридианец
Asparukh Akanayev from Calgary, AB, Canada
Alex J. Butler from United Kingdom

places.title: Lermontov Russian Drama Theatre
places.architect: G. Gorlyshkov, V. Davidenko, V. Rudenko, N. Shibalina
places.why: A modernist theatre of 1969 on Abai Avenue, home to the Russian drama company.

places.title: House of Soviets
places.why: A modernist administrative block of the 1960s on the main north–south avenue, shortlisted in 2026 for local heritage protection.

places.title: TsUM Department Store
places.architect: M. Gura, P. Mikhaldyk, T. Mironenko
places.why: The central department store of 1961, an early modernist glass box at the head of the Arbat, shortlisted for heritage protection.

places.title: Monolithic houses in Samal
places.why: A late-Soviet housing group of cast-in-place concrete by Almas Ordabaev, an attempt to give mass housing more freedom of form.

places.title: Philippov House
places.why: A merchant’s house of 1901 from the Verny era, a monument of republican significance.

places.title: Kazpotrebsoyuz Building
places.why: A post-war classical office building on the Old Square, which it frames together with the House of Government.

places.title: Central Stadium
places.architect: Alexander Leppik, A. Kapanov, A. Kosov
places.why: The main stadium of the city, opened in 1958, at the foot of the mountains along Abai Avenue.

places.title: Musrepov Youth Theatre (former Auezov Theatre)
places.architect: Alexander Leppik, Nikolai Ripinsky, Vladimir Katsev
places.why: An early modernist theatre of 1962, built for the Kazakh drama company before it moved to its new house on Abai Avenue.

photos.file: Казахский государственный академический театр для детей и юношества имени Г. Мусрепова (Алматы) - panoramio.jpg
photos.author: Николай Максимович

places.title: Hotel Alatau
places.architect: I. Kushnarev, S. Temirgaliev, A. Petrov
places.why: A tourist hotel of 1975 on the upper Dostyk Avenue, a long slab listed as a local monument.

places.title: Hotel Dostyk
places.why: A late-Soviet hotel for official guests near Hotel Kazakhstan, listed as a local monument.

places.title: KIMEP University (former Higher Party School)
places.architect: D. Kim, D. Melnikov, B. Voronin et al.
places.why: The former Higher Party School of 1978, a campus of concrete blocks at the corner of Abai and Dostyk avenues, now an English-language university.

places.title: Satbayev University main building
places.why: The main building of the polytechnic, a late-Soviet composition shortlisted in 2026 for local heritage protection.

places.title: Kirov Plant housing
places.why: Post-war apartment houses of the Kirov machine-building plant in a modest classical style, shortlisted in 2026 for local heritage protection.

places.title: House of the Zenkov architects
places.why: The home of Pavel Zenkov and his son Andrei, the builders of the cathedral and of much of Verny; a monument of republican significance.

places.title: Gavrilov House
places.why: An Art Nouveau merchant’s house built for the owner of the Semirechye tobacco factory, listed at republican level.

places.title: Verny Observatory
places.why: A small brick observatory of 1915 with the tower of the Bredikhin astrograph.

places.title: Tenir Eco Hotels
places.why: Prefabricated modular cabins on the mountainside at about 3200 m, near the top of the Shymbulak lifts, placed with little disturbance to the slope and reached by gondola.

places.title: Kazakh State Circus
places.why: A round circus under a ribbed dome that recalls the frame of a yurt, landed like a flying saucer among the trees of Abai Avenue.

places.title: Kazakh TV Studio Complex
places.why: A brutalist broadcasting centre of 1983, praised as a rare blend of Central Asian tradition and modern architecture; its exterior has been kept.

places.title: Auezov Kazakh Drama Theatre
places.architect: O. Baimurzaev, Arystan Kainarbaev, M. Zhaksylykov
places.why: A brutalist theatre of 1980 for the Kazakh drama company; its architects received the State Prize of the Kazakh SSR.

places.title: House of Friendship
places.architect: L. Timchenko, Rustem Seidalin, Kh. Yakupbaev
places.why: A modernist building whose round conference hall is shaped like a yurt; the leaders of the former Soviet republics signed the Alma-Ata Declaration here in December 1991.

places.title: Aul housing complex
places.architect: B. Voronin, L. Andreyeva, Yuri Ratushny et al.
places.why: A late-Soviet housing complex of bulbous, colourful forms around linked courtyards, named after the Kazakh word for village.

places.title: Sairan Bus Station
places.why: A late-Soviet bus terminal of 1983 by Lake Sairan, added to the local heritage list in 2021.

places.title: Zholdasbekov Palace of Students
places.architect: V. Bondarenko, V. Egorov, Yu. Zimin
places.why: A late-Soviet cultural centre on the university campus, with a large hall, listed as a local monument.

places.title: Alatau Sanatorium
places.architect: Yuri Ratushny, Oleg Balykbaev, V. Sidorov, Tokhtar Eraliev
places.why: A large late-Soviet health resort in the foothills on the western edge of the city, now a hotel; listed as a local monument.

places.title: Gorky Central Park
places.why: The oldest and largest park of the city, 47 hectares of old trees, ponds and alleys at the end of Gogol Street, where families spend their weekends.

photos.file: Центральный парк культуры и отдыха им. М.Горького - Центральный Вход - panoramio.jpg
photos.author: A.Makarenkov

places.title: First President’s Park
places.why: A large landscaped park on the southern slope with a colonnaded entrance, cascades of fountains and views to the mountains, one of the favourite walks of the city.

photos.file: Japanese Garden in the Park of the First President in Almaty.jpg
photos.author: Wetowp5029

places.title: Baum Grove
places.why: A 3.5 km forest, mostly of elms, planted by the forester Eduard Baum on the northern edge of the city, crossed by straight alleys and renewed in 2026.

places.title: Terrenkur
places.area: along the Malaya Almatinka, Dostyk Avenue to Tattimbet Street
places.why: A walking trail of about 4 km along the Malaya Almatinka river under old trees, renewed in 2025 with a wooden bridge, a white rotunda, a pond and an amphitheatre.

places.title: Esentai river promenade
places.why: A riverside promenade of about 4 km along the Esentai, a long green corridor for walking and cycling through the southern districts.

places.title: Yuzhny Park
places.why: A 16-hectare neighbourhood park in the south of the city, renewed in 2026.

places.title: Lake Sairan
places.area: between Tole bi Street and Abai Avenue
places.why: A reservoir on the Bolshaya Almatinka ringed by a promenade, a favourite place for evening walks, rebuilt as a public space in 2022–2026.

photos.file: Вид на озеро Сайран с работавшим фонтаном.JPG
photos.author: Kalabaha1969

places.title: Atakent (former Exhibition of Achievements)
places.why: The former exhibition grounds of Soviet Kazakhstan: a park of pavilions with an entrance arch, now a place for walks with a square renewed in 2026.

photos.file: 2012 Вид на горы из парка Атакента 01.jpg
photos.author: Екатерина Борисова

places.title: Tulebaev Street
places.why: A quiet street of the old centre shaded by tall trees and lined with memorial plaques of the people who lived here.

places.title: Kazakhconcert (former House of Political Education)
places.why: A post-war building of 1955 in red stone, with tall pilasters and carved ornament, built for political education and later home to the philharmonic and the Kurmangazy folk orchestra; a monument of republican significance.

photos.file: Здание Казахской Государственной филармонии (Дом политпросвещения), проспект Абылай хана, 83, Алма-Ата.jpg
photos.author: SAKRI

places.title: Baum House
places.why: The house of the forester Eduard Baum, who planted the grove that bears his name and much of the green of Verny.

places.title: Mukhtar Auezov House Museum
places.why: The house and garden of the writer Mukhtar Auezov on Tulebaev Street, a villa of a Soviet intellectual of the 1950s kept as a museum since his death in 1961; a monument of republican significance.

photos.file: Muhtar Auez murajai uiinin artky jagy.jpg
photos.author: Bekbal

places.title: Akhmet Baitursynuly House Museum
places.why: The last home of Akhmet Baitursynuly, the reformer of the Kazakh alphabet, a modest house of the late Verny era kept as a museum; a monument of republican significance.

photos.file: Akhmet Baytursynov's memory museum in Almaty.JPG
photos.author: МаратД
